title: Weekly skill scout
instructions:
Scout for new skills worth adding to my MimiWork, and prepare them for my review.

1. Search the web for Claude/agent skills published or trending in the LAST 7 DAYS: GitHub (search 'claude skill' and 'SKILL.md' sorted by recent stars, plus the awesome-claude-skills lists), X posts about new agent skills, and newsletters or blogs announcing them. Cast wide — slides, documents, charts, research, data analysis, design.
2. For each candidate, open the repository and judge it on substance: a real SKILL.md, instructions that would actually change my output (not a thin wrapper), and evidence of care (examples, evals, recent commits). Skip anything that merely restates what a model does by default.
3. CHECK THE LICENSE before recommending anything. MIT/Apache/BSD are fine. Note copyleft. Flag anything Noncommercial or all-rights-reserved as 'look, do not copy' — those must never be bundled or auto-installed.
4. Compare against the skills I already have (list them first) — do not recommend near-duplicates of installed skills; if a candidate clearly supersedes an installed one, say so.
5. Write a report saved as the deliverable: for each pick — name, link, license, what it does, why it earns a place, and a one-line install note. Order by how much it would improve my actual work (research, teaching, slides, writing). Three excellent picks beat ten mediocre ones; say plainly if a week produced nothing worth adding.
6. For the single best MIT/Apache-licensed pick, ALSO save a ready-to-review copy: fetch its SKILL.md and any small essential reference files into a folder named after the skill inside the workspace. Do NOT install anything into my skills — the report and the draft folder are for me to review and decide.
